chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from one of our companions — whom I think was al-Sayyārī — from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, who said:

When Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā (عليه السلام) came to al-Mahdī, he saw him restoring wrongfully taken rights. So he said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, why is our grievance not being redressed?” He said to him, “And what is that, O Abū al-Ḥasan?” He said: “When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, granted to His Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) Fadak and what was around it, no cavalry or riding beasts had been sent against it.”
So Allah sent down upon His Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله): “And give the near relative his due.”

But the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) did not know who they were, so he referred that matter to Jibrāʾīl, and Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) referred it to his Lord. Then Allah revealed to him: “Hand over Fadak to Fāṭimah (عليها السلام).” So the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) called her and said to her: “O Fāṭimah, Allah has commanded me to hand over Fadak to you.” She said: “I have accepted, O Messenger of Allah, from Allah and from you.”

Her agents remained in it during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله). Then when Abū Bakr assumed authority, he expelled her agents from it. So she came to him and asked him to return it to her. He said to her: “Bring me a black or a red one to testify for you concerning that.” So she brought Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) and Umm Ayman, and they testified for her. Thus he wrote for her an order that there be no interference.

She left with the document in her possession, and ʿUmar met her and said: “What is this with you, O daughter of Muḥammad?” She said: “A document that Ibn Abī Quḥāfah wrote for me.” He said: “Show it to me.” But she refused, so he snatched it from her hand, looked at it, then spat in it, effaced it, and tore it up. Then he said to her: “Your father did not send cavalry or riding beasts against this, so put ropes around our necks.”

Then al-Mahdī said to him: “O Abū al-Ḥasan, define its boundaries for me.” He said: “One boundary of it is Mount Uḥud, another boundary of it is al-ʿArīsh of Egypt, another boundary of it is the seacoast, and another boundary of it is Dūmat al-Jandal.” He said to him: “All of this?” He said: “Yes, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, all of this. All of this is among that over whose people the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) did not advance with cavalry or riding beasts.” He said: “It is much, and I will consider it.”

key_terms.الْمَظَالِمَ: wrongfully taken rights or grievances being restored
key_terms.بِتَرْكِ التَّعَرُّضِ: an order to refrain from interference
key_terms.بِخَيْلٍ وَلَا رِكَابٍ: without military advance by cavalry or mounts, indicating fayʾ
key_terms.ذَا الْقُرْبَىٰ: the near relative entitled to a divinely assigned due
key_terms.فَدَكًا: the property of Fadak granted to Fāṭimah (عليها السلام)
key_terms.وُكَلَاؤُهَا: her agents or representatives managing the property

ai.seo_question: How does the hadith of Imām Mūsā al-Kāẓim (عليه السلام) explain the issue of Fadak and its connection to the verse about giving the near relative his due?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates Imām Mūsā al-Kāẓim (عليه السلام) presenting the grievance of Fadak before al-Mahdī and recounting that it was granted by divine command to Fāṭimah (عليها السلام). It also connects the grant of Fadak to the Qur'anic command to give the near relative his due and portrays the later dispute over its possession and scope.
